chunks: And he narrated it through another route, with wordings that add and omit compared to what preceded. He narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from his father, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: The people narrate among us that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted like this and this and this—and he gestured with his hand, placing one palm over the other—ten and ten and nine, more often than he fasted like this and this and this, meaning ten and ten and ten.

He said: So Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast fewer than thirty days, and the month of Ramadan has not decreased from thirty days since Allah created the heavens and the earth.

key_terms.السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ: the heavens and the earth; an expression indicating primordial creation
key_terms.تِسْعًا: nine; indicating the count of twenty-nine days
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ: thirty; the number affirmed in the report for the fasting month
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah; the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan; the obligatory month of sawm (fasting)
key_terms.صَامَ: fasted; refers here to the observance of the Ramadan fast
key_terms.عَشْرًا: ten; used in counting the days by hand gesture

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ever fast Ramadan for only twenty-nine days according to this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a question to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام about reports concerning whether the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days or thirty days. The Imam replies by affirming that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast less than thirty days and that Ramadan has not been deficient from thirty days since Allah created the heavens and the earth.
